All of Us is written in a deeply committed and compassionate way, but although I agree with its political points, and am moved by some of its scenes, I also think that it’s not entirely problem-free.

cn.t: Martinez's debut play delivers authentic, fiery criticism of disability welfare cuts with humor and raw anger, but critics split on its effectiveness—some find it urgent and moving, others say it's overlong, repetitive, and more polemic than drama.
